Surface recreation leak: native PSS grows approximately 12 MB per HOME/relaunch surface cycle despite destroy-complete markers and an explicit Device::Destroy experiment. Root cause requires further Dawn/Skia lifecycle investigation.

surface_recreation_leak_check.command: Five HOME -> relaunch surface recreation cycles with dumpsys meminfo after each cycle; then force-stop and inspect logcat.
surface_recreation_leak_check.markers: 8 SurfaceRuntime destroy complete events and 9 Dawn initialized events; no FATAL EXCEPTION or Fatal signal.
surface_recreation_leak_check.native_pss_kb: ~30,584 before the first probe; ~129,689 after eight cycles (about +12 MB per recreation).
surface_recreation_leak_check.follow_up_experiment: Two temporary teardown experiments were tested and reverted: wgpu::Device::Destroy() before Dawn handle release, and Skia Context::freeGpuResources() after synchronous completion. Neither changed the observed growth: a five-cycle run still rose from 42,969 KB to 92,549 KB native PSS. The experiments are not part of the committed five-file Android scope.
surface_recreation_leak_check.classification: GPU lifecycle is functional, but repeated surface recreation retains substantial native memory. The growth persists after explicit Dawn device destruction and Skia resource purging, so full B3 leak acceptance is failed and the root cause likely requires common Dawn/Skia or emulator-driver investigation outside this isolated five-file Android slice.
